column5: Every name on my list is someone I saved.
And not one of them came back.
I'm Mark. Chicago has been dark for eight days.
Last night, I found a video of me turning the city off.
So I climbed out of the tunnel to find out why.
The man from the radio was waiting by the trucks.
Welcome back, Mark. We were worried about you.
He handed me a badge. My face. My name.
City Grid Control. Night supervisor.
And the second I touched it, I remembered.
Day one. Every screen in the control room went red.
Something had gotten into the grid.
It moved through the wires. House to house.
Wherever a light was on.
And the people inside those houses,
stopped being people.
So we turned the city off. Block by block.
To starve it.
And I wrote down everyone it hadn't reached yet.
That was the list. The ones we got out.
The last name I wrote was Mrs. Alvarez's grandson.
Your notebook, Mark. The pages you didn't write.
Nobody on your list is in that tunnel.
So ask yourself who's been writing to you.
I opened the notebook.
There was a new line. The pencil still fresh.
Don't trust him. Look at his eyes.
I looked up.
His eyes were lit. From the inside.
